title: Exact interlayer triplet-pairing eigenstates in the extended Hubbard model
abstract: $η$-pairing symmetry generalizes the pairing mechanisms in superconductivity but is broken in the presence of interlayer interactions. In this work, we extend this approach to triplet pairs. We propose interlayer triplet-pairing operators for the multi-layer extended Hubbard model. We find that a set of exact condensate-pair eigenstates can be constructed, which exhibit off-diagonal long-range order. In contrast to the $η$-pairing mechanism, this originates from restricted spectrum generating algebra and is only available for bilayer and trilayer systems in the presence of interlayer Hubbard interactions. Nevertheless, the system also retains the original on-site $η$-pairing symmetry in the absence of interlayer interactions. Consequently, both singlet and triplet pairs coexist in the eigenstates of the multi-layer Hubbard model. We employ quench dynamics to demonstrate the results through numerical simulations. Our findings open avenues for the study of exact condensate-pair states in strongly correlated systems.
summary: The authors propose and derive exact interlayer triplet-pairing eigenstates for the multi-layer extended Hubbard model. These unique states only exist in bilayer and trilayer systems due to specific constraints on the Hamiltonian's algebra. The study confirms these states via time evolution simulations, highlighting a coexistence of singlet and triplet pairing mechanisms.
main_problem: The work investigates the existence and properties of exact interlayer triplet-pairing eigenstates within the multi-layer extended Hubbard model, extending prior knowledge on $\eta$-pairing states.
main_result: Exact condensate-pair eigenstates exhibiting off-diagonal long-range order are found for bilayer and trilayer systems when interlayer interactions are present. These states demonstrate a unique pairing mechanism distinct from the standard $\eta$-pairing symmetry.
method: The analysis relies on constructing these exact eigenstates by analyzing commutation relations involving the Hamiltonian and specialized triplet-pairing operators, utilizing a Restricted Spectrum Generating Algebra (RSGA).
model_or_system: The system is the multi-layer extended Hubbard model defined on a 2D square lattice with parameters including intralayer hopping ($t$), interlayer hopping ($t_\perp$), on-site repulsion ($U$), and interlayer interaction ($V$). The Hamiltonian incorporates both singlet ($\eta$) and triplet ($\zeta$) pairing channels.
key_observables: Off-diagonal long-range order (ODLRO), fidelity $F(t)$ under time evolution, and correlation functions for singlet ($C_S$) and triplet ($C_T$) pairs.
important_parameters: The existence of exact states is critically dependent on the number of layers ($\lambda=2$ or $\lambda=3$) and the presence of interlayer interactions ($V \neq 0$).
main_assumptions: The derivation requires restricting Hamiltonian parameters to satisfy the conditions necessary for applying the Restricted Spectrum Generating Algebra (RSGA).
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates that the fidelity $F(t)$ remains unity for $\lambda=2, 3$ when $V \neq 0$, while decaying for $\lambda=4$. Figure 3 shows correlation functions decaying when interlayer interactions are present.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the model and operators, derives the conditions for exact eigenstates using RSGA, proves their existence only for bilayer/trilayer systems, and finally uses quench dynamics simulations (fidelity analysis) to confirm these theoretical findings.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous analytical framework for finding exotic, long-range ordered states in strongly correlated lattice models, which is highly relevant for understanding high-$T_c$ superconductivity mechanisms beyond simple mean-field treatments.
